sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在这里，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上奇异美妙的事物，同时提升你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today it’s the start of our next three-part mini-series, this time on the theme of “university”.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天是我们全新三集迷你系列的开篇，本系列的主题是“大学”。

sentences.en: In part one, today’s episode, we’ll go on a whirlwind journey through the history of universities and higher education, from the Medieval period to the present day.
sentences.zh: 在今天的第一集里，我们将开启一段旋风般的旅程，回顾从中古时期到当今的大学与高等教育历史。

sentences.en: In part two, we’ll zoom in and talk about universities in the UK, the different types of universities, what life is like at a British university, and I’ll share a load of my personal experience too, as I spent a total of five years studying at universities in the UK.
sentences.zh: 在第二集里，我们将把镜头拉近，聊聊英国的大学、不同类型的大学、英国大学的生活是什么样的，我还会分享我个人的大量经历，因为我在英国的大学总共度过了五年的学习时光。

sentences.en: And in part three, the final part, we’ll talk about something that said it was a university, but was later accused of being a complete fraud: Trump University.
sentences.zh: 而在第三集，也就是最后一部分，我们将聊聊一个自称是大学、但后来被指控为彻头彻尾的骗局的机构：Trump University。

sentences.en: OK then, let's not waste a minute and get right into it.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们一分钟也不要浪费，直接切入正题吧。

sentences.en: There are practically no institutions that have survived for 1,000 years.
sentences.zh: 几乎没有任何机构能够存活一千年。

sentences.en: The Vatican City only goes back just over 700, the “ancient” city of Machu Picchu is not yet 600 years old, and even sandwiches have only been around for 250.
sentences.zh: 梵蒂冈的历史也才刚过 700 年出头，“古城”马丘比丘还不到 600 岁，就连三明治也才出现 250 年而已。

sentences.en: Yet in just over 60 years’ time, one institution will celebrate its 1,000 year anniversary.
sentences.zh: 然而在仅仅 60 多年之后，一个机构将庆祝它的千禧年诞辰。

sentences.en: The University of Bologna is, by some measures, the world’s oldest university.
sentences.zh: 博洛尼亚大学在某种程度上是世界上最古老的大学。

sentences.en: It was founded in the year 1088, some 937 years ago.
sentences.zh: 它建于公元 1088 年，距今已有 937 年的历史。

sentences.en: If you go there today, the university doesn’t seem very old, or at least it doesn’t look so different from the rest of the city.
sentences.zh: 如果你今天去那里，这所大学看起来并不是非常古老，或者至少它看起来和这座城市的其他地方没有太大区别。

sentences.en: But of course, 1,000 years ago, it was very different.
sentences.zh: 但当然，在 1,000 年前，情况大不相同。

sentences.en: It bore little resemblance to any modern university: no sprawling campus, no central library, no stone quadrangles where students wandered around in gowns.
sentences.zh: 它与任何现代大学几乎毫无相似之处：没有错落有致的校园、没有中央图书馆、也没有穿着长袍的学生闲逛的石头方庭。

sentences.en: In fact, the “university” was more of an idea than a formal structure; it was really an informal gathering of young men who congregated in the same place and hired older, more learned men to instruct them.
sentences.zh: 事实上，“大学”与其说是一个正式的结构，不如说是一个概念；它其实是一群年轻人的非正式聚会，他们聚集在同一个地方，并雇佣年长、更有学问的人来教导他们。

sentences.en: Now, before we get into how this worked in practice, and what they were studying, we should address the question of “why?”.
sentences.zh: 现在，在我们探讨这在实践中是如何运作的以及他们当时在学什么之前，我们应该先探讨一下“为什么”这个问题。

sentences.en: Why then, and why there? Why do we see universities springing up in the 11th, 12th and 13th centuries?
sentences.zh: 为什么是在那个时候，又为什么是在那个地方？为什么我们在 11、12 和 13 世纪会看到大学如雨后春笋般涌现？

sentences.en: Why in Europe in particular? Well, a few things were happening at once.
sentences.zh: 为什么偏偏是在欧洲？嗯，当时有几件事同时在发生。

sentences.en: Europe in the 11th and 12th centuries was finally becoming a little more stable.
sentences.zh: 11 世纪和 12 世纪的欧洲终于变得更加稳定了一些。

sentences.en: Populations were growing, towns were expanding, and trade was starting to flourish.
sentences.zh: 人口在增长，城镇在扩张，贸易开始蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: In places like northern Italy, new city-states were booming with merchants, bankers and notaries.
sentences.zh: 在意大利北部等地，新兴的城邦里商贾云集，银行家和公证人活跃。

sentences.en: These were societies that needed contracts, charters, and legal expertise.
sentences.zh: 这些都是需要合同、特许状和法律专业知识的社会。

sentences.en: At the same time, something extraordinary happened.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，一件非同寻常的事情发生了。

sentences.en: Through contact with the Islamic world, in Spain, Sicily, and during the Crusades, European scholars rediscovered long-lost works of ancient philosophers, physicians, and thinkers.
sentences.zh: 通过与西班牙、西西里以及在十字军东征期间与伊斯兰世界的接触，欧洲学者重新发现了古希腊哲学家、医师和思想家长期失传的著作。

sentences.en: In Bologna, a copy of Justinian’s Corpus Juris Civilis, the great code of Roman law, re-emerged.
sentences.zh: 在博洛尼亚，查士丁尼的《民法大全》（一部伟大的罗马法典）的副本重新浮出水面。

sentences.en: This was alongside works of Aristotle, the great Greek physician Galen, and more.
sentences.zh: 这与亚里士多德、伟大的希腊医师盖伦等人的著作一起出现。

sentences.en: Suddenly, there was a sophisticated body of knowledge just waiting to be studied.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，出现了一套复杂的知识体系正等待着人们去研究。

sentences.en: The Catholic Church was also a huge factor.
sentences.zh: 天主教会也是一个巨大的因素。

sentences.en: It was the single most powerful institution in Europe, owning vast amounts of land, collecting taxes, and even running its own courts.
sentences.zh: 它是欧洲唯一最具权力的机构，拥有大量的土地，征收税款，甚至运营着自己的法庭。

sentences.en: Historically, it had been where knowledge and learning was confined to.
sentences.zh: 从历史上看，知识和学问一直被局限在教会里。

sentences.en: Monks were practically the only group in society that could read and write; books had to be meticulously copied by hand, by monks, of course, and these sources of knowledge were kept in monasteries, often under lock and key.
sentences.zh: 修士几乎是社会中唯一能够读写的人；书籍必须由修士一笔一划地精心抄写，当然，这些知识的来源被保存在修道院里，通常是锁在柜子里的。

sentences.en: But by this point, the church’s needs had evolved.
sentences.zh: 但到了这个时候，教会的需求已经演变了。

sentences.en: To manage its sprawling empire it needed more than just monks who could pray and copy manuscripts.
sentences.zh: 为了管理其庞大的帝国的需要，它需要的不仅仅是会祈祷和抄写手稿的修士。

sentences.en: It needed educated clergy: men trained not only in theology but also in law, philosophy, and the practical business of administration.
sentences.zh: 它需要受过教育的神职人员：不仅接受过神学培训，还接受过法律、哲学和行政管理实际业务培训的人。

sentences.en: So, on the one hand you had these booming towns and ambitious rulers who wanted lawyers and administrators.
sentences.zh: 所以，一方面你有这些蓬勃发展的城镇和雄心勃勃、需要律师和行政人员的统治者。

sentences.en: On the other, you had the Church demanding skilled administrators and legal experts.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，你有要求熟练的行政人员和法律专家的教会。

sentences.en: And in the middle, you had rediscovered texts of Roman law and classical philosophy providing the material to study.
sentences.zh: 而在中间，你拥有被重新发现的罗马法和古典哲学文本，为研究提供了材料。

sentences.en: It was a case of right time, right place.
sentences.zh: 这就是天时、地利、人和。

sentences.en: Now, importantly, these early universities weren’t “founded” in the sense we might think of today.
sentences.zh: 现在，重要的是，这些早期的大学并不是我们今天所理解的那种“创立”的。

sentences.en: It wasn’t the Church or a king who founded the University of Bologna.
sentences.zh: 并不是教会或某位国王创立了博洛尼亚大学。

sentences.en: It was the students themselves. They banded together in guilds, pooled their money, and hired masters to teach them.
sentences.zh: 是学生自己。他们组成行会，凑钱雇佣学者来教他们。

sentences.en: This is what “universitas” originally meant, not “a university” as we think of today, but a corporation of students.
sentences.zh: 这就是“universitas”最初的意思，不是我们今天认为的“大学”，而是学生的法人团体。

sentences.en: And what gave these communities staying power, the ability to continue year after year, was recognition from the pope.
sentences.zh: 而赋予这些社区持久力、能够年复一年延续下去的能力，是教皇的承认。

sentences.en: Popes issued charters granting universities privileges, such as exemption from local taxes, the right to be tried in church courts, and most importantly, the authority for their degrees to be recognised across Christendom.
sentences.zh: 教皇颁发特许状，授予大学特权，例如免除地方税收、在教会法庭受审的权利，以及最重要的一点，他们的学位在整个基督教世界得到承认的权威。

sentences.en: In other words, someone could take their degree from the University of Bologna and show it to their master in Paris, and it would be recognised as valid.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，某人可以拿着他们在博洛尼亚大学获得的学位，向他们在巴黎的导师展示，并且该学位将被认为有效。

sentences.en: Now, in terms of what students would study at these universities, the curriculum was surprisingly uniform.
sentences.zh: 现在，就学生在这些大学里学习的内容而言，课程出奇地统一。

sentences.en: A young man, and they were almost always men, would typically begin with what was known as the trivium: grammar, rhetoric, and logic.
sentences.zh: 一个年轻人（而且几乎总是年轻人）通常会从所谓的“三艺”开始：语法、修辞学和逻辑学。

sentences.en: In practical terms, this meant first mastering Latin, which was the language of the church.
sentences.zh: 在实践中，这意味着首先要精通拉丁语，这是教会的语言。

sentences.en: Then, mastering how to craft an argument and deliver a speech.
sentences.zh: 然后，掌握如何构建论点和发表演讲。

sentences.en: And then it was logic: the art of reason, evaluating statements logically and systematically.
sentences.zh: 接着是逻辑学：推理的艺术，合乎逻辑且系统地评估陈述。

sentences.en: It wasn’t so different from some of the skills that you might have learned at university.
sentences.zh: 这与你在大学里可能学到的一些技能并没有太大区别。

sentences.en: And once the young man had mastered those, he would move on to the quadrivium: arithmetic, geometry, music, and astronomy.
sentences.zh: 一旦年轻人掌握了这些，他就会进入“四艺”：算术、几何、音乐和天文学。

sentences.en: Together, these seven subjects made up the so-called “liberal arts,” which were the foundation of medieval higher education.
sentences.zh: 这七门学科共同构成了所谓的“自由艺术”，它们是中世纪高等教育的基础。

sentences.en: After this, the most ambitious and wealthy students could progress to the higher faculties of law, medicine, and theology.
sentences.zh: 在此之后，最有野心和最富有的学生可以进入更高阶的法学、医学和神学系。

sentences.en: And, not unlike the modern day, different universities excelled at different subjects.
sentences.zh: 而且，与现代没有什么不同，不同的大学在不同的学科上表现卓越。

sentences.en: Law was especially important at Bologna, theology dominated in Paris, and medicine was strong in places like Salerno.
sentences.zh: 法学在博洛尼亚尤为重要，神学在巴黎占主导地位，而医学在萨勒诺等地则很强。

sentences.en: Degrees could take years, even decades, to complete, and many students never finished, again, not so dissimilar to some modern universities.
sentences.zh: 获得学位可能需要数年甚至数十年的时间，许多学生从未毕业，这再次说明，这与某些现代大学并没有太大不同。

sentences.en: And by the 13th and 14th centuries, universities had appeared in Oxford, Cambridge, Salamanca, Padua, Prague, and Heidelberg.
sentences.zh: 到了 13 和 14 世纪，牛津、剑桥、萨 Salamanca、帕多瓦、布拉格和海德堡都出现了大学。

sentences.en: Wherever they were founded, they became magnets for ambitious men and symbols of prestige for the rulers who would often sponsor them, paying for their fees and living expenses, with the expectation that they would return and serve them after they graduated.
sentences.zh: 无论它们建在哪里，它们都成为雄心勃勃的男人们的磁石，也是通常会资助它们的统治者的威望象征，统治者会支付他们的学费和生活费，期望他们在毕业后能够回来为自己服务。

sentences.en: A little like an employer today paying for someone to go and do an MBA.
sentences.zh: 这有点像今天的雇主出钱让人去读 MBA。

sentences.en: After all, for these young men, there was a clear incentive to go to university.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，对于这些年轻人来说，去上大学有明显的动力。

sentences.en: Mastering Roman and canon law wasn’t just an intellectual exercise; it was a ticket to a career as a notary, a judge, or an adviser to a bishop or prince.
sentences.zh: 精通罗马法和教会法不仅仅是一场智力锻炼；它是通往公证人、法官或主教或亲王顾问等职业的入场券。

sentences.en: In a society where almost all power was mediated through law or the Church, education became a pathway to influence, and one that was worth paying for.
sentences.zh: 在一个几乎所有权力都通过法律或教会来调解的社会里，教育成了通往影响力的途径，而且这是一条值得付钱去走的道路。

sentences.en: Now, although by the 14th century or so, universities were well-established, and there were around 50 scattered across Europe, they still only educated an extreme minority of the population, so we’re probably talking about fewer than 50,000 students at every university in total.
sentences.zh: 现在，尽管到了 14 世纪左右，大学已经相当成熟，欧洲各地散落着大约 50 所大学，但它们仍然只教育了极少数的人口，所以我们可能在讨论所有大学总共不到 50,000 名学生。

sentences.en: And most graduates would become clergyman, priests, or some form of administrator within the church or a city state system.
sentences.zh: 大多数毕业生会成为神职人员、牧师，或者教会或城邦系统中的某种行政人员。

sentences.en: But as Europe moved into the Renaissance, universities began to change.
sentences.zh: 但随着欧洲进入文艺复兴时期，大学开始发生变化。

sentences.en: Instead of focusing almost entirely on theology and law, a new movement of scholars known as humanists championed the studia humanitatis: the study of grammar, rhetoric, history, poetry, and moral philosophy.
sentences.zh: 人文主义者这一新学派没有几乎完全集中在神学和法律上，而是倡导人文科学（studia humanitatis）：对语法、修辞学、历史、诗歌和道德哲学的研究。

sentences.en: These were subjects drawn from the classical world, inspired by the rediscovery of Greek and Roman texts.
sentences.zh: 这些学科取材于古典世界，受到对希腊和罗马文本重新发现的启发。

sentences.en: They shifted the focus away from purely preparing men for service in the church or the courtroom, and towards shaping a more rounded, critical, and eloquent citizen.
sentences.zh: 他们的重点从纯粹为教会或法庭服务培养人才，转变为塑造一个更全面、更有批判精神、更有口才的公民。

sentences.en: Then came the Scientific Revolution, and with it, the university became a place not only for preserving existing knowledge but also for producing it.
sentences.zh: 随后科学革命到来，随之而来的是，大学不仅成为保存现有知识的地方，也成为了产生知识的地方。

sentences.en: Now, this is an important distinction to make.
sentences.zh: 现在，这是一个需要做出的重要区别。

sentences.en: For the first four to five centuries, universities were places for students to learn from the current corpus of knowledge; there was no focus whatsoever on discovery, of challenging accepted knowledge and research to uncover new ideas.
sentences.zh: 在前四到五年的时间里，大学是学生向现有知识体系学习的地方；根本没有关注发现，没有挑战被接受的知识和研究来揭示新想法。

sentences.en: Science, of course, is all about pushing human understanding forward, questioning why the world is how it is.
sentences.zh: 科学，当然，全都是关于推动人类理解向前发展，质疑世界为什么是这个样子。

sentences.en: If you were Galileo Galilei at the University of Padua, in Italy, this meant asking yourself whether the sun goes around the Earth or the Earth goes around the sun.
sentences.zh: 如果你是意大利帕多瓦大学的伽利略，这意味着要问自己是太阳绕着地球转还是地球绕着太阳转。

sentences.en: If you were Sir Isaac Newton in Cambridge, in England, this meant asking what causes an apple to fall from the sky.
sentences.zh: 如果你是英国剑桥大学的艾萨克·牛顿爵士，这意味着要探究是什么导致苹果从空中落下。

sentences.en: It might sound obvious, especially now when a large chunk of a university lecturer’s time is supposed to be dedicated to research, but at the time, it wasn’t.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能很显眼，特别是现在大学讲师很大一部分时间应该投入到研究中，但在当时并非如此。

sentences.en: And by the 18th and 19th centuries, universities were being reshaped again, pushing them even further towards what we see today.
sentences.zh: 到了 18 和 19 世纪，大学再次被重塑，将它们进一步推向了我们今天看到的样子。

sentences.en: In Berlin, Wilhelm von Humboldt developed a new model: the idea that research and teaching should go hand in hand, that scholars should be free to pursue knowledge wherever it might lead.
sentences.zh: 在柏林，威廉·冯·洪堡开发了一种新模式：研究和教学应该齐头并进，学者应该可以自由地追求知识，无论它通向何方。

sentences.en: This so-called “Humboldtian” model spread quickly and influenced universities across Europe, and later the United States.
sentences.zh: 这种所谓的“洪堡”模式迅速传播，并影响了整个欧洲以及后来的美国的大学。

sentences.en: It is, of course, the basis for much of modern higher education.
sentences.zh: 当然，它是现代高等教育大部分的基础。

sentences.en: Universities should educate young, curious minds, but they should also be centres of research and discovery.
sentences.zh: 大学应该教育年轻、好奇的心灵，但它们也应该成为研究和发现的中心。

sentences.en: So, by this point, at the turn of the 20th century, there were something like 200 universities worldwide, depending on exactly what you classify as a university.
sentences.zh: 所以，到了这个时候，即 20 世纪之交，全球大约有 200 所大学，这取决于你究竟如何将大学分类。

sentences.en: The student body had also expanded, but there were still only around 500,000 university students worldwide, a tiny fraction of the estimated 250 million students today.
sentences.zh: 学生群体也扩大了，但全球依然只有大约 50 万名大学生，这只是今天估计的 2.5 亿学生的一小部分。

sentences.en: University was still exclusive, expensive, and an option only for a tiny sliver of society.
sentences.zh: 大学仍然具有排他性、昂贵性，而且只是社会一小撮人的选择。

sentences.en: This all started to change in the post-war period, when governments across the developed world invested heavily in higher education.
sentences.zh: 这一切在战后时期开始改变，当时发达国家的政府大力投资高等教育。

sentences.en: In the United States, the GI Bill gave returning soldiers the chance to go to college.
sentences.zh: 在美国，《退伍军人权利法案》让复员军人有机会上大学。

sentences.en: In Europe, new universities opened their doors for a generation hungry for opportunity.
sentences.zh: 在欧洲，新大学为渴望机会的一代人敞开了大门。

sentences.en: And across Asia, Africa, and Latin America, universities were established as symbols of independence, progress, and modernity.
sentences.zh: 在亚洲、非洲和拉丁美洲，大学被建立为独立、进步和现代性的象征。

sentences.en: For the first time in history, higher education was no longer the preserve of a tiny elite.
sentences.zh: 这是历史上第一次，高等教育不再是一小撮精英的专属领地。

sentences.en: And that brings us to the modern day. There is no single accepted figure for the number of universities worldwide, with estimates ranging from 25,000 to 50,000, educating an estimated 250 million students.
sentences.zh: 这就把我们带到了现代。目前没有一个普遍接受的全球大学数量的数据，估计从 25,000 到 50,000 不等，教育着大约 2.5 亿学生。

sentences.en: It is, for many professions, still an almost mandatory requirement, making university a necessary next step after school.
sentences.zh: 对许多职业来说，它仍然是一项几乎强制性的要求，使得上大学成为学校教育之后必要下一步。

sentences.en: In the UK, like most countries, getting a “good” job is significantly harder without a university degree, and the better the university you went to, and the better grades you got, the more likely you are to find a good job after graduation.
sentences.zh: 在英国，像大多数国家一样，没有大学学位想要找到“好”工作要困难得多，而且你上的大学越好，取得的成绩越好，毕业后找到好工作的可能性就越大。

sentences.en: There are plenty of counter-examples to this, of self-made millionaires who dropped out of school and carved their own path to success, but these are anomalies, in the UK at least.
sentences.zh: 对此有大量的反例，比如辍学并开辟自己成功之路的白手起家的百万富翁，但这些只是反常现象，至少在英国是这样。

sentences.en: If you look through the CV or Wikipedia page of almost anyone who has achieved “career success” in some form of professional environment, you will almost certainly find the name of a reputable university on there.
sentences.zh: 如果你翻阅几乎任何在某种职业环境中取得“职业成功”的人的简历或维基百科页面，你几乎肯定会在上面找到一所信誉良好的大学的名字。

sentences.en: And in the UK, successive British governments have pushed to get as many young people into university as possible, proclaiming that the percentage of people graduating from university is a success metric.
sentences.zh: 在英国，历届英国政府一直在推动尽可能多的年轻人上大学，宣称大学毕业生的百分比是一个成功指标。

sentences.en: High = good, low = bad. In 1997, Tony Blair famously stated that he wanted 50% of British young people to go to university.
sentences.zh: 高就是好，低就是坏。1997年，托尼·布莱尔曾名言指出，他希望 50% 的英国年轻人能够上大学。

sentences.en: At the time, it was seen as ambitious, almost utopian.
sentences.zh: 在当时，这被视为雄心勃勃，甚至是乌托邦式的。

sentences.en: It took 20 years, but in 2017, it happened.
sentences.zh: 花了 20 年时间，但在 2017 年，它实现了。

sentences.en: 50.2% of young people in the UK went on to higher education.
sentences.zh: 英国 50.2% 的年轻人接受了高等教育。

sentences.en: And in fact, if you removed men from the equation, the target would have been hit much faster, as only 44% of men go on to higher education while 57% of women do.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你把男性从等式中剔除，这个目标会更快达到，因为只有 44% 的男性接受高等教育，而女性则为 57%。

sentences.en: Now, 50% is significant, and moving above 50% means it’s something most people do.
sentences.zh: 现在，50% 是一个重要的数字，超过 50% 意味着这是大多数人都会做的事情。

sentences.en: And if it is something that most people do, it has, by definition, become less valuable.
sentences.zh: 如果这是大多数人都会做的事情，那么根据定义，它变得不那么有价值了。

sentences.en: And students are no longer studying the trivium: grammar, rhetoric, and logic, or at least, most aren’t.
sentences.zh: 而且学生们不再学习三艺：语法、修辞和逻辑，或者至少，大多数人没有。

sentences.en: There has been a boom in vocational courses, courses that teach students practical skills and prepare them for a particular job or career: hospitality management, journalism, and so on.
sentences.zh: 职业课程出现了蓬勃发展，这些课程向学生传授实用技能，并为他们从事特定的工作或职业做好准备：酒店管理、新闻学等等。

sentences.en: And the criticism of many of these courses is that, perhaps ironically, they don’t do a very good job at preparing students for the professional world.
sentences.zh: 对许多这类课程的批评是，也许具有讽刺意味的是，它们在让学生为职业世界做准备方面做得并不好。

sentences.en: A degree in “golf management” might sound perfect for a 17-year-old fan of golf, but the reality is that it probably isn’t even the best course to study if they want to work in the golf industry.
sentences.zh: 一个“高尔夫管理”学位对一个 17 岁的高尔夫迷来说听起来很完美，但现实是，如果他们想在高尔夫行业工作，它可能甚至不是最好的学习课程。

sentences.en: And alongside this, we must mention the cost.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，我们还必须提及成本。

sentences.en: As you might remember from episode number 513, on the UK university crisis, the cost of university has expanded dramatically in the UK.
sentences.zh: 正如你可能从关于英国大学危机的第 513 期节目中记得的那样，英国的大学费用急剧膨胀。

sentences.en: Before 1997, it was free, and it has risen to almost €10,000 per year today.
sentences.zh: 在 1997 年之前，它是免费的，而今天已经上涨到每年近 10,000 欧元。

sentences.en: It is expensive, and that’s before you factor in the cost of living as a student.
sentences.zh: 它很昂贵，这还不算你作为学生的生活成本。

sentences.en: Indeed, according to a report that came out this summer, the average student in the UK graduates with £53,000 in debt, around €60,000.
sentences.zh: 事实上，根据今年夏天发布的一份报告，英国普通学生毕业时背负着 53,000 英镑的债务，约为 60,000 欧元。

sentences.en: Interestingly enough, this is actually more than the average student in the US.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，这实际上比美国的普通学生还要多。

sentences.en: The difference is that the cost of tuition in the US varies wildly, so the most expensive degrees at the most prestigious American universities can cost over $100,000 a year, while some universities can be completely free.
sentences.zh: 不同之处在于，美国的学费差异很大，因此美国最负盛名的大学里最昂贵的学位一年可能要花费 100,000 多美元，而有些大学可能是完全免费的。

sentences.en: In the UK, the best university can cost the same as the worst university, which leads to the situation that everyone has relatively equal high costs, but of course, not everyone graduates with degrees of equal value, which is something we’ll talk more about in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 在英国，最好的大学和最糟糕的大学花费可能是一样的，这就导致了这样一种情况：每个人的相对高昂成本是平等的，但当然，并不是每个人毕业时获得的学位价值都是相等的，这是我们将在下一集中更多讨论的事情。

sentences.en: Now, to wrap up this exploration of higher education through time, I want to leave you with one last thought, and that’s about things that have and haven’t changed over the almost 1,000 years of the existence of university.
sentences.zh: 现在，为了总结这次对贯穿时间的的高等教育的探索，我想留给你最后一个想法，那就是关于近 1000 年大学存在期间已经改变和未改变的事物。

sentences.en: One theme is the university student’s perpetual feeling of not having enough money.
sentences.zh: 一个主题是大学生永远感觉没有足够的钱。

sentences.en: It’s understandable; students are, theoretically speaking, too busy studying to work, and with often hefty tuition fees to pay and rent to make, history is filled with examples of students complaining about being short on cash.
sentences.zh: 这是可以理解的；理论上讲，学生忙于学习而无法工作，并且经常要支付高昂的学费和房租，历史上充满了学生抱怨手头紧的例子。

sentences.en: Something that might have changed, however, is students' priorities about what they spend their money on.
sentences.zh: 然而，可能已经改变的是学生对自己花钱之事的优先顺序。

sentences.en: So I’ll leave you with a quote from one 15th-century Dutch student, Desiderius Erasmus Roterodamus, or Erasmus of Rotterdam, as he is most commonly known.
sentences.zh: 所以我将用一位 15 世纪的荷兰学生德西德里乌斯·伊拉斯谟·罗特罗达穆斯（Desiderius Erasmus Roterodamus），也就是人们更熟知的鹿特丹的伊拉斯谟的一句名言来结束。

sentences.en: He famously said, “When I have a little money, I buy books; and if I have any left, I buy food and clothes.”
sentences.zh: 他有一句名言：“当我有一点钱时，我买书；如果还有剩的，我买食物和衣服。”

sentences.en: If Erasmus were a student today, I wonder whether he would still have the same priorities…
sentences.zh: 如果伊拉斯谟今天是名学生，我不知道他是否还会有相同的优先顺序……

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode on the history of universities.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天的大学历史节目就到这里。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one and that you've learnt something new, at least something you might not have learned at university.
sentences.zh: 我希望这期节目很有趣，并且你学到了一些新东西，至少是一些你可能在大学里没学过的新知识。

sentences.en: As a reminder, this is part one of a three-part mini-series on the theme of “university”.
sentences.zh: 提醒一下，这是关于“大学”主题的三集迷你系列的第一部分。

sentences.en: Next up, in part two, we’ll be talking about universities in Britain: the different types of universities, the application process, university culture, and what life is like if you choose to study at a British university.
sentences.zh: 接下来，在第二部分，我们将讨论英国的大学：不同类型的大学、申请流程、大学文化，以及如果你选择在英国大学学习生活会是什么样的。

sentences.en: And in part three, we’ll also be talking about something that called itself a university, but got into a lot of trouble for doing so: Trump University, and the scandal that followed.
sentences.zh: 在第三部分，我们还将讨论一个自称是大学但因此惹上大麻烦的机构：Trump University，以及随之而来的丑闻。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，请注意安全，我们下期节目再见。
